chapter: Trombone technique, plunger mute and the California years
title: Blending in a section and the role of the lead
summary: Sections blend if players balance volume; only the lead should stand out slightly.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: In terms of things like playing in bands, playing in sections, when the instruments were not matched... I mean, you see that they look different, and maybe one guy is playing a cornet and has a long bore trumpet and so on... Was that harder in the past than it is now?
To get a good blend in a section and stuff.
Was it harder what? You mean...
You mean did we... Did the band blend?

They blended if the guys played them right. Sure, they blended. They blended just fine, if the guys played them right. Some guys, though, would blow their horn and make it too loud for the other horns. You know? And you're all supposed to blend together and make it all come out with the same volume. That's what you want, the right volume of each instrument so each can be heard, not that you overshadow this other instrument.

Yeah. The only thing that's supposed to stand out a little louder than any of them is the lead. It's got to stand out just a little louder than the others. But not too much louder. Because if he blasts, the other guy is going to blast. You know?
